class.name: Netw
class.brief_description: Static entry points for the Networked API.
class.description:
Each method resolves the [NetwMultiplayer] associated with its node argument. Use [method of] to access that session directly. [codeblock] Netw.session(self).participants # who is playing Netw.clock(self).tick # the tick every peer shares Netw.scene(self).admit(participant) # let a player into a world Netw.spawn(_spawn_bullet, dir) # make a node on every peer Netw.rpc(turret.aim, yaw) # call a method on every peer [/codeblock] [b]Joining a session[/b] Connecting a [MultiplayerPeer] starts the network connection. [method join] requests a place in the game and returns a [NetwParticipant]. It may be called before or after assigning [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer]; an offline session queues the request. [codeblock] func host() -> void: var peer := ENetMultiplayerPeer.new() peer.create_server(21253) Netw.join(self, &"Mario", [&"red"]) multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = peer [/codeblock] The server runs the handler declared by [method configure_join] once for every join it accepts. Its first parameter is always the [NetwParticipant] the session seated, and its remaining parameters are the extra values [method join] was given. Those parameter types are how both sides agree on what those values are, so the handler is a named method rather than a lambda. What the handler returns is where the player ends up. Returning a [NetwSceneHandle] puts the player in that world and lets them in, as one act. Returning nothing means the handler placed the player itself, which is what the example below does. Returning a [NetwPromise] makes the session wait for it and then read what it carries as one of the other two. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_join(self, seat_player)
func seat_player(participant: NetwParticipant, team: StringName) -> void: arena.add_child(Netw.spawn_player(participant, _spawn_avatar, team)) [/codeblock] A session declaring no handler falls back to [NetwDefaultJoin]. A rejected join announces as [signal NetwConnectHandle.join_failed]. The seat this peer was given is [member NetwSessionHandle.local_participant], filled at [signal NetwSessionHandle.local_joined]. [b]The tick[/b] Every peer in a session counts the same tick, and it is the time everything networked is stamped with. [method clock] reaches it. [method configure_clock] chooses how fast it runs, and a session that declares nothing has no clock at all. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_clock(self).tickrate(60)
@onready var clock := Netw.clock(self)
func _ready() -> void: clock.before_tick.connect(_read_input) clock.on_tick.connect(_simulate) [/codeblock] [signal NetwClockHandle.before_tick] is where a player's input is read and [signal NetwClockHandle.on_tick] is where the tick is simulated, which is the order prediction and lag compensation both assume. [NetwClockHandle] is the whole clock. [b]Declare in _init[/b] Declare from [method Object._init] and never from [method Node._ready]. A spawned node is addressable through its [member NetwEntity.route] before [method Node._ready] runs, so a declaration made there can arrive after the first packet it was meant to govern. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state().quantize( NetwQuantizeScalar.new().limits(-64.0, 64.0).step(0.01), )
func _ready() -> void: # too late. the first position for this node may already have # arrived and been read on the wrong grid pass [/codeblock] [b]Replicated Properties[/b] [method configure_property] declares a variable's delivery once, and the variable is written normally afterwards. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state() # sent every tick Netw.configure_property(self, &"fuel") # sent when pushed
func refuel() -> void: fuel = 100.0 Netw.sync_property(self, &"fuel") [/codeblock] [NetwPropertyConfig] is everything a field can be told about how it travels, and [enum NetwPropertySet.Record] is where [method NetwPropertyConfig.state], [method NetwPropertyConfig.input] and [method NetwPropertyConfig.broadcast] are compared. [b]RPCs, requests and signals[/b] A call is addressed by [member NetwEntity.route] rather than by a node path, so it never errors on a node that has not spawned yet, and it reaches only the peers that see the entity. Godot's [code]@rpc[/code] supplies the authority mode and the transport. [method configure_rpc] registers the method and declares what the annotation has no spelling for, such as a [method NetwMemberConfig.controller] write policy or a [NetwQuantize] per argument. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_rpc(self.aim).controller().quantize( NetwQuantizeAngle.new().bits(12).centered(), )
@rpc("any_peer", "unreliable") func aim(yaw: float) -> void: turret.rotation.y = yaw [/codeblock] A request is an RPC with a response. [method request] calls the server, [method request_id] calls one peer, and [method request_all] calls every client through a [NetwGroupPromise]. Each method returns a promise. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_rpc(self.buy)
@rpc("any_peer", "reliable") func buy(item: StringName) -> bool: return wallet.spend(item)
var sold: bool = await Netw.request(shop.buy, &"shield").wait() [/codeblock] A signal replicates the same way once [method configure_signal] allowlists it, except that it emits on the local sender too. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_signal(self.exploded)
Netw.emit_entity_signal(self.exploded, position) [/codeblock] A [NetwEntity] or entity root [Node] passed as an argument crosses the wire as its [member NetwEntity.route] and arrives live on the far side. An [Array] in trailing position is one argument, never an argument list. Bytes belonging to no entity at all go through a [method channel] instead. [b]Spawning and despawning[/b] A spawn function runs on every peer and constructs from its arguments alone, so it is registered like an RPC and called like one. The caller parents what [method spawn] returns, and [method despawn] removes the entity everywhere. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_spawn(_spawn_bullet)
func _spawn_bullet(dir: Vector2) -> Node: var bullet := BULLET.instantiate() bullet.setup(dir) return bullet [/codeblock] [codeblock] muzzle.add_child(Netw.spawn(_spawn_bullet, dir)) # server only Netw.despawn(bullet) [/codeblock] The arguments decide what is built and a field marked [method NetwPropertyConfig.on_spawn] carries what it was holding, applied on the other peers once the function has run. [method spawn_player] is the same act for the node a player drives, and it fills [member NetwEntity.controller] before the node enters the tree so the node leaves with its peer. [method replicate] is the door for a node the game instantiated itself, which is where loading a saved player belongs. [b]Scenes[/b] A multiplayer scene is a world a player is let into. [method configure_multiplayer_scene] declares one, every node under it belongs to it, and a player receives what is inside only once [method NetwSceneHandle.admit] has let them in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_multiplayer_scene(self).labeled(&"Arena") [/codeblock] [codeblock] var arena := Netw.scene(self, &"Arena") # by label, or Netw.scene(self) arena.admit(participant) arena.player_entered.connect(_on_car_entered) [/codeblock] A game opens a world by spawning it and admitting players to it, and it can also travel players the way the engine travels a scene. [method change_scene_to_file] is that second shape made multiplayer correct, since [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_file] moves this peer alone and leaves the rest of the session running without it. The [enum SceneChange] scope says who the change is for. The server's own call applies straight away. A client's call is a request, and an arriving request is rejected unless [method configure_scene_requests] declared a handler that admits it. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_scene_requests(self, authorize)
func authorize(who: NetwParticipant, destination: String, _scope: int) -> Error: return OK if unlocked(who, destination) else ERR_UNAUTHORIZED
await Netw.change_scene_to_file( self, "res://match.tscn", Netw.SCENE_CHANGE_PARTICIPANT).wait() [/codeblock] [b]Interest[/b] A [NetwInterestLayer] decides which peers are told about which entities, so what a player cannot see is never sent to them at all. Every peer declares the layers a node belongs to, and the server owns the real membership and the viewers. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_interest(self) \ .join(&"team:red", NetwMultiplayer.LEAVE_POLICY_RETAIN) \ .on_enter(_on_seen) [/codeblock] [codeblock] var sight := Netw.of(self).interest_layer(&"sight") # server only sight.add_entity(NetwEntity.of(target)) sight.add_viewer(peer_id) [/codeblock] [NetwInterestLayer] holds the membership and the signals that report it, and [NetwInterestHandle] is the same declaration read back from [member NetwEntity.interest]. [b]Prediction[/b] A predicted node runs the same simulation locally that the server will run, so it moves the moment a player presses something instead of a round trip later. The property marks are what make that possible. A [method NetwPropertyConfig.input] field is what this peer authors and replays, and a [method NetwPropertyConfig.state] field is what the server corrects when the two disagree. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: var entity := Netw.configure_entity(self) entity.initial_controller = NetwEntity.INITIAL_REPRESENTED_PEER entity.prediction.archetype = NetwPredict.ARCHETYPE_KINEMATIC
Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state().on_spawn() Netw.configure_property(self, &"move_dir").input() [/codeblock] [NetwPredictionHandle], reached as [member NetwEntity.prediction], holds every prediction setting one node has and the evidence of its last comparison. [NetwPredict] names the values those settings are written with. [b]Interpolation[/b] A node driven by another peer arrives a few times a second and is drawn every frame, so what a player sees is smoothed between the values that arrived. [method NetwMemberConfig.interpolate] declares how one value is smoothed. [member NetwEntity.interpolation] holds what is true of the whole node, such as the [member NetwDisplayHandle.visual_root] that receives the smoothed writes while the body keeps its own. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_entity(self).interpolation.visual_root = ^"Sprite" Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state().interpolate( NetwInterpolate.new().lerp().smooth(0.05), ) [/codeblock] [NetwInterpolate] is the spec for one value and [NetwDisplayHandle] is the one for the whole node. [b]Lag compensation[/b] The server keeps what every node held over the last few seconds, so a shot can be judged against the world the shooter was actually looking at rather than the one that has arrived since. [method sample] reads one node's past. [method rewind] puts a set of them back for the length of one call and always restores the present afterwards. [codeblock] func _fire(ctx: NetwActionContext) -> void: var past := Netw.sample(target_entity, ctx.view_tick) if not past.has_value(&"position"): ctx.deny() [/codeblock] [method action] is the same idea for a one-off act such as firing or placing something. It plays the effect declared on [member NetwAction.predict] right away, sends the server a request it judges at [member NetwActionContext.view_tick], and takes the effect back when the server returns [method NetwActionContext.deny]. [method configure_lagcomp] only tunes this, since the recording starts itself as soon as anything asks for it. [codeblock] @onready var place_bomb := Netw.action(_place_bomb)
func _place_bomb(ctx: NetwActionContext) -> void: var bomb := BOMB.instantiate() ctx.bind(bomb) bombs.add_child(bomb) [/codeblock] [b]Everything else[/b] The sections above are what a game needs in order to play. Each row below is something else this addon owns, and the class named is where it is documented. - [NetwConnectHandle] building a peer and listing the servers to connect to - [NetwAuthFlow] admission, deciding who is let in at all - [NetwSessionHandle] who is playing, and the session's state - [NetwChannel] bytes belonging to no node - [NetwService] one part of a game reaching another without a node path - [NetwDatabase] persistence, saving a field and loading it back - [NetwSchema] many rows of one shape, sent and stored together as a table - [ParticipantViewport] split screen, several players sharing one machine, one viewport each - [LocalLoopbackSession] local testing, a whole session running in one process - [NetwMultiplayer] the verbs, the flat call behind every door on this class

method.name: action
change_scene_to_file
method.description: Travels players to [param path] the way [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_file] travels this peer, except that the rest of the session comes along. [param scope] says who is travelling, and it means the same thing whoever calls it. [constant SCENE_CHANGE_SESSION] brings everyone, [constant SCENE_CHANGE_PARTICIPANT] brings one player and leaves every world standing, and [constant SCENE_CHANGE_SCENE] brings whoever is in the world [param node] sits in. The server's own call applies. A client's call is a request that [method configure_scene_requests] decides, so a session declaring no handler rejects it. [codeblock] var err: Error = await Netw.change_scene_to_file( self, "res://match.tscn").wait() if err != OK: status.text = "Could not start the match." [/codeblock]

method.name: change_scene_to_packed
method.description: The same travel as [method change_scene_to_file], from a [PackedScene] that came from a file. A [PackedScene] built in memory is rejected, because a client can only ask for a scene by path.

method.name: channel
method.description: A [NetwChannel] for sending bytes that belong to no node, such as voice or chat. [param channel_id] runs from [code]100[/code] to [code]254[/code], and both peers open the same number to talk to each other. [codeblock] var voice := Netw.channel(self, 100) voice.broadcast(frame, false) [/codeblock]

method.name: clock
method.description:
The [NetwClockHandle] of the session [param node] is in, which is the tick every peer counts together. A session has one clock, so every caller in it is handed the same handle and a component may connect once and keep it. [signal NetwClockHandle.before_tick] is where input is read and [signal NetwClockHandle.on_tick] is where the tick is simulated. [codeblock] @onready var clock := Netw.clock(self)
func _ready() -> void: clock.before_tick.connect(_sample_input) clock.on_tick.connect(_simulate) [/codeblock] [method configure_clock] is where the clock is set up before the session starts. This is how a running one is reached.

method.name: configure_auth
method.description:
Declares how this session checks that a player is who they claim to be, by naming a [param factory] that builds its [NetwAuthFlow]. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_auth(self, make_auth)
func make_auth() -> NetwAuthFlow: var flow := NakamaAuth.new() flow.bind_session(NakamaSessionService.of(self)) flow.bind_tree(self) return flow [/codeblock] A flow usually needs something the game already holds, such as the login service it verifies against, so [param factory] is where the flow is built and wired in one place. [member NetwSessionHandle.auth_flow] reaches the built flow afterwards for anything that cannot be known at declaration. Declare it from [method Object._init] on a node in the session's branch. [param factory] takes no arguments and returns a fresh [NetwAuthFlow]. It runs once for the session, at the first login that needs it rather than at declaration, and the session keeps what it built even after the declaring node is gone. A session declaring nothing lets players in on the username they claim. A [param factory] returning anything else turns every login down rather than falling back to that. Pass [code]Callable()[/code] to clear the declaration.

method.name: configure_clock
method.description: Sets up the clock of the session [param node] belongs to, and returns the [NetwClockConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_clock(self) \ .tickrate(60) \ .display_offset(2) [/codeblock] Declaring this is what starts the clock. From then on the session steps it once per physics frame, and a rig that wants to step the ticks itself turns that off with [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_MANUAL_TICK]. Declare it from [method Object._init]. A [param preset] is copied as it is taken, so chaining onto what comes back never edits a shared [code].tres[/code]. To fill it in from the inspector instead, hold the returned config in an exported field and declare from [method Node._enter_tree], since an exported value cannot be read during [method Object._init]. Declaring twice for one [param node] is an error and returns the first config unchanged. A value written after the session has read the config is reported and changes nothing. [NetwClockConfig] documents every field, and [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_config] is what the running session holds.

method.name: configure_despawn
method.description: Declares what the other peers do with [param node] when [method despawn] removes it, and returns the [NetwDespawnConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_despawn(self).linger(0.5) [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_entity
method.description: The [NetwEntity] for [param node], created if this is the first call, so the node can be set up before it exists on any other peer. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_entity(self).initial_controller = \ NetwEntity.INITIAL_REPRESENTED_PEER Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").on_spawn() [/codeblock] Call it from [method Object._init], while the node has no parent yet. It walks up to the topmost parentless node and puts the [NetwEntity] there, which is what makes a whole scene one entity rather than one per script. A node the tree already holds is past the moment one could be created for it, so it returns what [method NetwEntity.of] would. A component under a root with no script has no parents to walk during [method Object._init], so it declares at [constant Node.NOTIFICATION_PARENTED] instead. [method NetwEntity.of] is the everyday read and creates nothing. [method NetwEntity.ensure] puts the [NetwEntity] on the exact node given rather than walking up.

method.name: configure_interest
method.description: Declares which [NetwInterestLayer] groups [param node] belongs to, and returns the [NetwInterestHandle] that is also [member NetwEntity.interest]. Call it from [method Object._init] so every peer names the same groups and the same callbacks. The server decides the real membership. A group joined or left later goes through this same handle. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_interest(self) \ .join( \ &"team:red", \ NetwMultiplayer.LEAVE_POLICY_RETAIN, \ NetwMultiplayer.PERCEPTION_POLICY_HIDE, \ ) \ .join(&"sight") \ .on_enter(_on_interest_enter) [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_join
configure_lagcomp
method.description: Tunes how far back the session records what every node held, and returns the [NetwLagCompensationConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_lagcomp(self).input_gate_deadline_ticks(16) [/codeblock] This is optional. The recording starts itself as soon as a predicted node or a [NetwAction] needs it, using this config if one was declared and the defaults otherwise. Declare one to move a tick count off its default, or to bound the [NetwAction] traffic in a game that predicts nothing of its own. Once the session has read it there is no way to take it back, and the recording ends with the session. Declare it from [method Object._init]. A [param preset] is copied as it is taken, so chaining onto what comes back never edits a shared [code].tres[/code]. To fill it in from the inspector instead, hold the returned config in an exported field and declare from [method Node._enter_tree]. Declaring twice for one [param node] is an error and returns the first config unchanged. [NetwLagCompensationConfig] documents every field.

method.name: configure_multiplayer_scene
method.description: Makes [param node] a world players are let into one at a time, and returns the [NetwSceneConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_multiplayer_scene(self).labeled(&"Arena") [/codeblock] Every node under [param node] belongs to this world, and a player receives what is inside only once [method NetwSceneHandle.admit] has let them in. Call it from the scene root's [method Object._init], because this has to be true before the scene is sent to anyone. Nothing else about the node changes, so it still replicates its own properties. [method NetwSceneConfig.labeled] gives it a name [method scene] can look up, and [method NetwSceneConfig.isolated] gives it a physics world of its own. A node with no script returns [code]null[/code], since there would be nothing to hold the declaration.

method.name: configure_persistence
method.description: Declares where [param node] is saved and loaded, and returns the [NetwPersistenceConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_persistence(self) \ .database(preload("res://data/game.tres")) \ .table(&"players") Netw.configure_property(self, &"gold").persisted() [/codeblock] It names the database, the table, how often a snapshot is written and when a saved value is loaded back, for every field marked [method NetwPropertyConfig.persisted]. The server does the saving through [NetwPersistenceEngine], and [NetwPersistenceConfig] documents every field.

method.name: configure_property
method.description: Declares how [param property] travels between peers, and returns the [NetwPropertyConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_property(self, &"position").state() # sent every tick Netw.configure_property(self, &"fuel") # sent when pushed, by the server Netw.configure_property(self, &"steering").controller() # sent when pushed, by the driver [/codeblock] A plain declaration only opens the field to [method sync_property]. Marking it [method NetwPropertyConfig.state], [method NetwPropertyConfig.input] or [method NetwPropertyConfig.broadcast] puts it in a set the session sends every tick, with no send call in the gameplay code at all. The declaration belongs to the script rather than to the node, so every instance declares the same thing from [method Object._init]. Pass [code]false[/code] for [param warn_late] when a field is only ever received and drawn, which is the one case where declaring after the node is in the tree races nothing.

method.name: configure_rpc
configure_scene_requests
method.description:
Declares who is allowed to ask this session to change scenes, which nothing else grants. [param handler] is given the [NetwParticipant] asking, the scene path they asked for, and the [enum SceneChange] they asked at. Returning [constant @GlobalScope.OK] lets it through and any other [enum Error] turns it down. The participant comes from the connection rather than from anything the client sent, so it cannot be claimed. A [param handler] returning something that is not an [enum Error] turns the request down and warns, which is how a broken one reads apart from a strict one. Only a client's request arrives here. The server's own [method change_scene_to_file] applies, on a dedicated server and on a listen host alike, so a game that drives every change from the server declares nothing and is never asked. A game that wants its host player held to the same rule calls its own check in both places. A session declaring nothing turns every request down and warns once. Two live declarations on one session do the same. Declare it from [method Object._init] on a node in the session's branch, and pass [code]Callable()[/code] to clear it. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_scene_requests(self, authorize_scene_request)
func authorize_scene_request( participant: NetwParticipant, destination: String, scope: int ) -> Error: if scope != Netw.SCENE_CHANGE_PARTICIPANT: return ERR_UNAUTHORIZED return OK if unlocked(participant, destination) else ERR_UNAUTHORIZED [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_schema
method.description:
Declares a [NetwSchema], which is a fixed set of named columns that many rows of the same shape are sent and stored as. This takes no node and reaches no session, because a schema is declared where the code using it lives, usually a [code]static var[/code] that runs before any session exists. Every session builds its own table from the same declaration, and declaring one name twice extends that one declaration rather than making a second. [codeblock] class Mobs: static var schema := Netw.configure_schema(&"Mob") static var pos := schema.vector3(&"pos") static var hp := schema.u16(&"hp")
var mobs := Netw.of(self).table_find(&"Mob") # the session's own handle [/codeblock] One declaration serves the replicated table, the properties bound to its columns, and [NetwDatabase]. A column holds a value of a fixed size, so anything of a length that varies goes on a [method channel] instead. [method NetwMultiplayer.table_commit] is how rows are published.

method.name: configure_server_info
method.description:
Declares what this server says about itself when a [NetwServerBrowser] asks. [param provider] is handed a [NetwServerInfo] already filled in from the session and returns what to send back, normally the same one with a few fields edited. A session with no provider uses [method NetwServerInfo.from_session]. Conflicting providers or an invalid return value report an error. Declare the provider from [method Object._init] on a node in the session branch. Pass [code]Callable()[/code] to clear it. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_server_info(self, server_info)
func server_info(info: NetwServerInfo) -> NetwServerInfo: info.motd = "Friday night session" info.max_players = 8 return info [/codeblock]

method.name: configure_session
method.description: Sets up the session [param node] belongs to, and returns the [NetwSessionConfig] to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_session(self) \ .app_id(&"bomber-v2") \ .desired_role(NetwMultiplayer.ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER) [/codeblock] The fields exported on a [MultiplayerTree] are only what a session falls back to when nothing declares this. Declaring it replaces those fields together rather than one at a time, so a tree field left out of the config is dropped and named once in a warning. Declare it from [method Object._init]. A [param preset] is copied as it is taken, so chaining onto what comes back never edits a shared [code].tres[/code]. To fill it in from the inspector instead, hold the returned config in an exported field and declare from [method Node._enter_tree], since an exported value cannot be read during [method Object._init]. Declaring twice for one [param node] is an error and returns the first config unchanged. A value written after the session has read the config is reported and changes nothing. [NetwSessionConfig] documents every field, and [method NetwMultiplayer.session_get_config] is what the running session holds.

method.name: configure_signal
method.description: Registers [param sig] so [method emit_entity_signal] may emit it on every peer, and returns the [NetwMemberConfig] that declares who is allowed to. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_signal(self.exploded) # only the server may emit it [/codeblock] A signal registered here defaults to [method NetwMemberConfig.call_local], so emitting it fires the local listeners as well. [method configure_rpc] and [method configure_property] default the other way, to [method NetwMemberConfig.call_remote].

method.name: configure_spawn
connection
despawn
method.description: Removes the node [method spawn] or [method replicate] made, on every peer. [codeblock] Netw.despawn(bullet) [/codeblock] [param opts] changes how this one removal goes, such as how long the node lingers before it is freed and whether what it held is saved first. [NetwDespawnOpts] documents every field, and [method configure_despawn] is where the same choices are declared once for a whole script. It returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] for a node that is not a spawned one and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] for a node in no session. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: emit_entity_signal
method.description:
Emits [param sig] on every peer, on that peer's copy of the same node, carrying the arguments given after it. Register the signal with [method configure_signal] first, which is also what decides whether this peer is allowed to emit it. A registered signal fires locally as well, so calling [code]sig.emit()[/code] beside this would fire the local listeners twice. [codeblock] Netw.emit_entity_signal(exploded) # local listeners AND every peer's copy
# only when the signal is configured .call_remote(): emit locally yourself exploded.emit() Netw.emit_entity_signal(exploded) # remote peers only [/codeblock]

method.name: join
method.description: Asks the session for a place in the game as [param username], carrying [param args] as the extra values the [method configure_join] handler takes after its [NetwParticipant]. [codeblock] Netw.join(self, &"Dev", [&"red"]) multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = peer [/codeblock] Call it before or after the peer is assigned. A session that is not online yet holds the request and sends it once it is, so the login cannot outrun it either way. Await the [NetwPromise] to tell a player their credentials were turned down before their connection is. A join that is turned down is reported whether or not the promise is read, and it announces as [signal NetwConnectHandle.join_failed]. An empty [param username] is rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER]. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: of
method.description: The [NetwMultiplayer] running the session [param node] is in, which is every session, entity, layer and display method under one object. [codeblock] var api := Netw.of(self) api.entity_despawn(route) [/codeblock] A node that is in no tree, and a node whose branch runs no session, both return [code]null[/code]. The rest of [Netw] is built on this, so [method session], [method clock], [method connection] and [method scene] return [code]null[/code] in the same two cases.

method.name: reload_current_scene
method.description: Travels back into the world this peer is already in, the way [method SceneTree.reload_current_scene] does, with the same [param scope] as [method change_scene_to_file]. The world is built again from scratch even though the path is the same, so a [NetwSceneHandle] held on the old one does not follow.

method.name: replicate
method.description: Sends a node the game built itself to every peer, which rebuild it from its [member Node.scene_file_path], and returns its [NetwEntity]. [param node] has no parent yet. [member NetwEntity.route], [member NetwEntity.entity_id], [member NetwEntity.peer_id] and [member NetwEntity.controller] are all filled in by the time this returns, and the other peers are not told anything until the node enters the tree. That gap is where a save is loaded and where the node's first values are written. [codeblock] var player := PlayerScene.instantiate() var entity := Netw.replicate(player, participant) await save.hydrate(entity) scene.add_child(player) [/codeblock] A node with no parent is in no session, so this one finds the only session running and reports an error when there is more than one. A host running several calls [method NetwMultiplayer.entity_replicate] on the one it means. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: request
method.description: Calls [param callable] on the server and returns a [NetwPromise] carrying what it returned. [codeblock] var sold: bool = await Netw.request(shop.buy, &"shield").wait() [/codeblock] Register the method with [method configure_rpc] first, the same as [method rpc].

method.name: request_all
method.description: Calls [param callable] on every peer that can see the node, and returns a [NetwGroupPromise] gathering what they each returned. Which peers are waited for is decided when the call goes out, so a peer arriving afterwards is not one of them. [NetwGroupPromise] is where one reply and the whole set are read.

method.name: request_controller
method.description: Calls [param callable] on the peer driving the node, its [member NetwEntity.controller], and returns a [NetwPromise] carrying what it returned.

method.name: request_id
method.description: Calls [param callable] on [param peer_id] alone and returns a [NetwPromise] carrying what it returned. A [param peer_id] of [code]0[/code] is rejected, since asking everyone is [method request_all].

method.name: rewind
method.description: Puts every node in [param entities] back where it was at [param tick], runs [param body] against that older world, then returns them all to where they are now. [codeblock] func _fire(ctx: NetwActionContext) -> void: var targets: Array[RID] = [] for other in Netw.scene(self).entities: targets.append(other.rid) Netw.rewind(targets, ctx.view_tick, _trace_shot) [/codeblock] Putting back and restoring always happen inside the one call, so the world is never left in the past. The session is found through [param body]'s own node, which is therefore a node in one. [method NetwMultiplayer.lagcomp_rewind] says what happens to a node with nothing recorded at [param tick].

method.name: rpc
method.description: Calls [param callable] on every peer that can see the node, carrying the arguments given after it. [codeblock] Netw.rpc(turret.aim, yaw) [/codeblock] Whether the call is reliable follows the method's own [code]@rpc[/code] annotation. Register it with [method configure_rpc] first. A [NetwEntity] or entity root [Node] passed as an argument arrives as that peer's own copy of it.

method.name: rpc_controller
method.description: Calls [param callable] on the peer driving the node, its [member NetwEntity.controller], and on nobody else.

method.name: rpc_id
method.description: Calls [param callable] on [param peer_id] alone, or on every connected peer when [param peer_id] is [code]0[/code].

method.name: sample
scene
method.description: The [NetwSceneHandle] for a world, which is how a game reads who is in it, lets players in, and hears when that changes. Left empty, [param named] means the world [param node] is in, which is also [member NetwEntity.scene]. Given a name, it means the one live world carrying that [method NetwSceneConfig.labeled] name, whether or not [param node] is inside it. A name identifies a kind of world, not an instance. If two live worlds share a name, the lookup fails. Use the handle returned when the world was spawned to select an instance. [codeblock] var here := Netw.scene(self) # the scene I am in var arena := Netw.scene(spawned) # the one I just spawned var track := Netw.scene(self, &"Track") # the only live Track [/codeblock]

method.name: service
method.description: The object the session is holding under [param type], which is how one part of a game reaches another without either knowing where it sits in the tree. [codeblock] var gamestate := Netw.service(self, MyGamestate) as MyGamestate [/codeblock] A session holding nothing under [param type] returns [code]null[/code], and so does one whose service has since been freed. [method service_register] and [method service_unregister] are the other two halves, and [method NetwMultiplayer.service_get] says what [param type] may be.

method.name: service_register
method.description: Hands [param service] to the session [param node] is in, so [method service] can find it under [param type], or under the service's own script when [param type] is left out. A [NetwService] does this for itself as it enters the tree and needs no call here. This is for an object a game keeps some other way, and for a node already sitting in the session that is becoming its service now.

method.name: service_unregister
method.description: Takes [param service] back from the session [param node] is in, so [method service] no longer finds it. A service withdrawing itself passes itself as both arguments, since [param node] says which session and [param service] says which object.

method.name: session
method.description: The [NetwSessionHandle] of the session [param node] is in, which is who is playing and what the session is doing. [codeblock] var s := Netw.session(self) s.entered.connect(_on_entered) s.disconnected.connect(_on_over) s.ended.connect(_on_over) [/codeblock] Every caller in one session is handed the same handle, so a game may connect these signals once and keep it. [Netw] is static and has no signals of its own, which is why they live here.

method.name: spawn
method.description: Builds the same node on every peer by running [param fn] with the arguments given after it, and returns this peer's copy for the caller to parent. [codeblock] muzzle.add_child(Netw.spawn(_spawn_bullet, dir, 2)) [/codeblock] Register [param fn] with [method configure_spawn] first. An [Array] after [param fn] is one argument rather than a list of them, an empty one included. The session is found through the node [param fn] lives on, so this works with any number of sessions running at once. [method spawn_player] is the same call for the node a player drives. What comes back is what [param fn] built, except for a world declared [method NetwSceneConfig.isolated], which comes back as the [SubViewport] holding it, since only a [Viewport] can own a physics world. Parent what comes back either way. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: spawn_player
method.description: Builds the node [param player] drives, the same way [method spawn] builds any other. [codeblock] players.add_child( Netw.spawn_player(player, _spawn_avatar, character_class) ) [/codeblock] It fills [member NetwEntity.peer_id] and [member NetwEntity.controller] from [param player] before the node enters the tree, so the node is counted as that player's and is removed when they disconnect. To remember who fired a bullet without making that bullet theirs to drive, pass the participant as an argument to [method spawn] instead. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: sync_property
method.description: Sends what [param property] is holding right now to the other peers, for a field that changes on events rather than every tick. [codeblock] func refuel() -> void: fuel = 100.0 Netw.sync_property(self, &"fuel") [/codeblock] Declare the field with [method configure_property] first, which is also what decides whether this peer is allowed to push it. The server sends it on to everyone, and a client asks the server to. A field marked [method NetwPropertyConfig.state], [method NetwPropertyConfig.input] or [method NetwPropertyConfig.broadcast] never needs this call, since the session is already sending it every tick.

constants.constant: Every participant converges on the destination and every other live scene retires. Whether a scene is isolated, how many are live, and whether authority also holds a local player do not change what this means.

One participant travels to the destination with the player entities it is enrolled in, and every world keeps running. A call with no participant to resolve is rejected rather than widened to the session.

The occupants of the one world the caller sits in travel to the destination and that world retires. Other worlds are untouched. Occupants means the participants whose [member NetwParticipant.current_scene] is that world, not the spectators admitted there while playing elsewhere.
The scene shares the physics and render world of whatever it is parented into.
The scene simulates in a world of its own, so geometry overlapping another scene's cannot interact with it.
